sanskrit: tataḥ sa vāry upaspṛśya kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ maitreyo dhārtarāṣṭraṃ tam aśapad duṣṭacetasam
english: Then Maitreya, his eyes reddened with anger, touched water and cursed that son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that evil-minded one.

sanskrit: yasmāt tvaṃ mām anādṛtya nemāṃ vācaṃ cikīrṣasi tasmād asyābhimānasya sadyaḥ phalam avāpnuhi
english: "Because you have disregarded me and refuse to heed these words, therefore receive at once the fruit of this arrogance."

sanskrit: tvadabhidrohasaṃyuktaṃ yuddham utpatsyate mahat yatra bhīmo gadāpātais tavoruṃ bhetsyate balī
english: "A great war shall arise born of enmity toward you, in which the mighty Bhīma shall shatter your thigh with blows of his mace."

sanskrit: ity evam ukte vacane dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ prasādayām āsa muniṃ naitad evaṃ bhaved iti
english: When these words had been spoken, King Dhṛtarāṣṭra sought to appease the sage, saying, "Let it not be so."

sanskrit: maitreya uvāca śamaṃ yāsyati cet putras tava rājan yathā tathā śāpo na bhavitā tāta viparīte bhaviṣyati
english: Maitreya said: "If your son, O king, pursues peace by any means, then the curse shall not come to pass; but if he acts otherwise, it shall."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa vilakṣas tu rājendra duryodhanapitā tadā maitreyaṃ prāha kirmīraḥ kathaṃ bhīmena pātitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Embarrassed, the father of Duryodhana then asked Maitreya, "O king of sages, how was Kirmīra slain by Bhīma?"

sanskrit: maitreya uvāca nāhaṃ vakṣyāmy asūyā te na te śuśrūṣate sutaḥ eṣa te viduraḥ sarvam ākhyāsyati gate mayi
english: Maitreya said: "I shall not tell it, for you bear jealousy, and your son does not heed my words. This Vidura will tell you everything once I have gone."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity evam uktvā maitreyaḥ prātiṣṭhata yathāgatam kirmīravadhasaṃvigno bahir duryodhano 'gamat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Maitreya departed by the way he had come; and Duryodhana, disturbed by the news of Kirmīra's slaying, went outside.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kirmīrasya vadhaṃ kṣattaḥ śrotum icchāmi kathyatām rakṣasā bhīmasenasya katham āsīt samāgamaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "O Kṣattā, I wish to hear of the slaying of Kirmīra — tell me how the encounter came about between Bhīmasena and that demon."

sanskrit: vidura uvāca śṛṇu bhīmasya karmedam atimānuṣakarmaṇaḥ śrutapūrvaṃ mayā teṣāṃ kathānteṣu punaḥ punaḥ
english: Vidura said: "Hear this deed of Bhīma, whose acts surpass human measure — I have heard it before in the accounts told of them again and again."

sanskrit: itaḥ prayātā rājendra pāṇḍavā dyūtanirjitāḥ jagmus tribhir ahorātraiḥ kāmyakaṃ nāma tad vanam
english: "From here, O king, the Pāṇḍavas departed after being defeated at dice, and within three days and nights they reached that forest called Kāmyaka."

sanskrit: rātrau niśīthe svābhīle gate 'rdhasamaye nṛpa pracāre puruṣādānāṃ rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām
english: "At midnight in the deep of night, O king, at the midpoint of that dreadful hour when man-eating demons of terrible deeds roam freely —"

sanskrit: tad vanaṃ tāpasā nityaṃ śeṣāś ca vanacāriṇaḥ dūrāt pariharanti sma puruṣādabhayāt kila
english: "— that forest the ascetics and other forest-dwellers always avoided from afar, out of fear of the man-eaters, it is said."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ praviśatāṃ tatra mārgam āvṛtya bhārata dīptākṣaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ rakṣaḥ solmukaṃ pratyadṛśyata
english: "As they entered there, O Bhārata, a fearsome demon with blazing eyes appeared blocking their path, carrying a firebrand."

sanskrit: bāhū mahāntau kṛtvā tu tathāsyaṃ ca bhayānakam sthitam āvṛtya panthānaṃ yena yānti kurūdvahāḥ
english: "He stood spreading his great arms wide and his terrible mouth agape, blocking the path along which the best of the Kurus were travelling."

sanskrit: daṣṭoṣṭhadaṃṣṭraṃ tāmrākṣaṃ pradīptordhvaśiroruham sārkaraśmitaḍiccakraṃ sabalākam ivāmbudam
english: "With lips and fangs gnashing, copper-red eyes, and hair blazing upright, he resembled a storm cloud charged with the rays of the sun and crackled with lightning."

sanskrit: sṛjantaṃ rākṣasīṃ māyāṃ mahārāvavirāviṇam muñcantaṃ vipulaṃ nādaṃ satoyam iva toyadam
english: "He unleashed demonic illusions and roared with a great tumultuous sound, releasing a vast rumble like a rain-laden cloud."

sanskrit: tasya nādena saṃtrastāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ sarvatodiśam vimuktanādāḥ saṃpetuḥ sthalajā jalajaiḥ saha
english: "Terrified by his roar, birds from every direction cried out and flew together in panic, those of the land joining those of the water."

sanskrit: saṃpradrutamṛgadvīpimahiṣarkṣasamākulam tad vanaṃ tasya nādena saṃprasthitam ivābhavat
english: "That forest, filled with fleeing deer, leopards, buffaloes and bears, seemed as though it were itself moving away at his roar."

sanskrit: tasyoruvātābhihatā tāmrapallavabāhavaḥ vidūrajātāś ca latāḥ samāśliṣyanta pādapān
english: "Struck by the great wind he raised, the reddish-leafed branches swayed, and creepers grown at a distance clasped the trees in embrace."

sanskrit: tasmin kṣaṇe 'tha pravavau māruto bhṛśadāruṇaḥ rajasā saṃvṛtaṃ tena naṣṭarṣkam abhavan nabhaḥ
english: "At that same moment a most dreadful wind blew; covered by the dust it raised, the sky lost its stars and became dark."

sanskrit: pañcānāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇām avijñāto mahāripuḥ pañcānām indriyāṇāṃ tu śokavega ivātulaḥ
english: "The great enemy, unrecognized by the five sons of Pāṇḍu, was like the incomparable surge of grief upon the five senses."

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavān dūrāt kṛṣṇājinasamāvṛtān āvṛṇot tad vanadvāraṃ maināka iva parvataḥ
english: "Seeing the Pāṇḍavas from afar clad in black antelope skins, he blocked the entrance to that forest like the mountain Maināka."

sanskrit: taṃ samāsādya vitrastā kṛṣṇā kamalalocanā adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ saṃtrāsān nyamīlayata locane
english: "Approaching him, the terrified Kṛṣṇā of lotus eyes, having never seen such a creature before, closed her eyes in fright."

sanskrit: duḥśāsanakarotsṛṣṭaviprakīrṇaśiroruhā pañcaparvatamadhyasthā nadīvākulatāṃ gatā
english: "With her hair still dishevelled and cast about by Duḥśāsana's hand, standing amidst the five mountains that were her husbands, she trembled like a river in flood."

sanskrit: momuhyamānāṃ tāṃ tatra jagṛhuḥ pañca pāṇḍavāḥ indriyāṇi prasaktāni viṣayeṣu yathā ratim
english: "As she was near to fainting, the five Pāṇḍavas caught hold of her, just as the senses hold fast to the pleasure dwelling in objects."

sanskrit: atha tāṃ rākṣasīṃ māyām utthitāṃ ghoradarśanām rakṣoghnair vividhair mantrair dhaumyaḥ samyakprayojitaiḥ paśyatāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ nāśayām āsa vīryavān
english: "Then the valiant Dhaumya, duly deploying various demon-slaying mantras, dispelled before the eyes of the sons of Pāṇḍu that terrible demonic illusion that had arisen."

sanskrit: sa naṣṭamāyo 'tibalaḥ krodhavisphāritekṣaṇaḥ kāmamūrtidharaḥ kṣudraḥ kālakalpo vyadṛśyata
english: "His illusion dispelled, the exceedingly powerful creature appeared in his true form — eyes wide with rage, assuming a shape of terrible desire, wicked and resembling death itself."

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato rājā dīrghaprajño yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ko bhavān kasya vā kiṃ te kriyatāṃ kāryam ucyatām
english: "Then the far-sighted King Yudhiṣṭhira addressed him: 'Who are you, and whose? What is your purpose here — tell us what must be done for you.'"

sanskrit: pratyuvācātha tad rakṣo dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram ahaṃ bakasya vai bhrātā kirmīra iti viśrutaḥ
english: "Then that demon replied to Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira: 'I am the brother of Baka, known by the name Kirmīra.'"

sanskrit: vane 'smin kāmyake śūnye nivasāmi gatajvaraḥ yudhi nirjitya puruṣān āhāraṃ nityam ācaran
english: "'I dwell in this desolate Kāmyaka forest at my ease, defeating men in battle and making them my daily food.'"

sanskrit: ke yūyam iha saṃprāptā bhakṣyabhūtā mamāntikam yudhi nirjitya vaḥ sarvān bhakṣayiṣye gatajvaraḥ
english: "'Who are you, arrived here as food for me? I shall defeat you all in combat and devour you without care.'"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu tac chrutvā vacas tasya durātmanaḥ ācacakṣe tataḥ sarvaṃ gotranāmādi bhārata
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira, having heard the words of that wicked one, then declared his clan, name and all the rest, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: pāṇḍavo dharmarājo 'haṃ yadi te śrotram āgataḥ sahito bhrātṛbhiḥ sarvair bhīmasenārjunādibhiḥ
english: "'I am Yudhiṣṭhira the Pāṇḍava, the Dharma-king — if the name has reached your ears — together with all my brothers Bhīmasena, Arjuna and the rest.'"

sanskrit: hṛtarājyo vane vāsaṃ vastuṃ kṛtamatis tataḥ vanam abhyāgato ghoram idaṃ tava parigraham
english: "'Having had my kingdom taken away and resolved to live in the forest, I have entered this dreadful forest that is your domain.'"

sanskrit: kirmīras tv abravīd enaṃ diṣṭyā devair idaṃ mama upapāditam adyeha cirakālān manogatam
english: "Kirmīra then said to him: 'By good fortune the gods have brought about for me today what I have long desired in my heart.'"

sanskrit: bhīmasenavadhārthaṃ hi nityam abhyudyatāyudhaḥ carāmi pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ nainam āsādayāmy aham
english: "'For the sake of killing Bhīmasena I have always roamed the whole earth with weapon raised, yet have never come upon him.'"

sanskrit: so 'yam āsādito diṣṭyā bhrātṛhā kāṅkṣitaś ciram anena hi mama bhrātā bako vinihataḥ priyaḥ
english: "'By good fortune he who killed my brother — long sought and now encountered — is here; for it was by him that my dear brother Baka was slain.'"

sanskrit: vetrakīyagṛhe rājan brāhmaṇacchadmarūpiṇā vidyābalam upāśritya na hy asty asyaurasaṃ balam
english: "'In the house of Vetrakiya, O king, disguised in the form of a Brahmin, relying on the power of trickery — for he has no real strength of his own.'"

sanskrit: hiḍimbaś ca sakhā mahyaṃ dayito vanagocaraḥ hato durātmanānena svasā cāsya hṛtā purā
english: "'And Hiḍimba, my dear friend who roamed these forests, was slain by this wicked one, and his sister was carried off by him long ago.'"

sanskrit: so 'yam abhyāgato mūḍho mamedaṃ gahanaṃ vanam pracārasamaye 'smākam ardharātre samāsthite
english: "'This fool has entered my deep forest at our hour of roaming, when midnight has arrived.'"

sanskrit: adyāsya yātayiṣyāmi tad vairaṃ cirasaṃbhṛtam tarpayiṣyāmi ca bakaṃ rudhireṇāsya bhūriṇā
english: "'Today I shall repay that long-nurtured enmity, and I shall satisfy Baka with an abundance of his blood.'"

sanskrit: adyāham anṛṇo bhūtvā bhrātuḥ sakhyus tathaiva ca śāntiṃ labdhāsmi paramāṃ hatva rākṣasakaṇṭakam
english: "'Today, having freed myself from the debt to my brother and my friend alike, I shall attain the highest peace by slaying this thorn in the flesh of demons.'"

sanskrit: yadi tena purā mukto bhīmaseno bakena vai adyainaṃ bhakṣayiṣye paśyatas te yudhiṣṭhira
english: "'If Bhīmasena was formerly spared by Baka, today I shall devour him before your very eyes, Yudhiṣṭhira.'"

sanskrit: enaṃ hi vipulaprāṇam adya hatvā vṛkodaram saṃbhakṣya jarayiṣyāmi yathāgastyo mahāsuram
english: "'For having slain this mighty-souled Vṛkodara today and fully consumed him, I shall digest him as Agastya did the great demon.'"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dharmātmā satyasaṃdho yudhiṣṭhiraḥ naitad astīti sakrodho bhartsayām āsa rākṣasam
english: "Thus addressed, the righteous and truth-pledged Yudhiṣṭhira, angered, retorted 'This shall not be' and threatened the demon."

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhur ārujya tarasā druma daśavyāmam ivodviddhaṃ niṣpatram akarot tadā
english: "Then great-armed Bhīma, uprooting a tree swiftly, stripped it of leaves — a tree some ten fathoms tall that had been torn up."

sanskrit: cakāra sajyaṃ gāṇḍīvaṃ vajraniṣpeṣagauravam nimeṣāntaramātreṇa tathaiva vijayo 'rjunaḥ
english: "Likewise Vijaya Arjuna, in the space of a single moment, strung the Gāṇḍīva, weighty as the thunderbolt's impact."

sanskrit: nivārya bhīmo jiṣṇuṃ tu tad rakṣo ghoradarśanam abhidrutyābravīd vākyaṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti bhārata
english: "Waving Jiṣṇu aside, Bhīma rushed at that demon of dreadful aspect and called out the words 'Stand! Stand!' O Bhārata."

sanskrit: ity uktvainam abhikruddhaḥ kakṣyām utpīḍya pāṇḍavaḥ niṣpiṣya pāṇinā pāṇiṃ saṃdaṣṭoṣṭhapuṭo balī tam abhyadhāvad vegena bhīmo vṛkṣāyudhas tadā
english: "Having spoken thus, the mighty Pāṇḍava charged at him in fury, pressing his girdle tight, cracking palm against palm, with lips bitten, wielding the tree as his weapon — so Bhīma rushed upon him with speed."

sanskrit: yamadaṇḍapratīkāśaṃ tatas taṃ tasya mūrdhani pātayām āsa vegena kuliśaṃ maghavān iva
english: "Then he brought it crashing down upon his head with speed, like the thunderbolt of Maghavan, resembling the staff of Yama."

sanskrit: asaṃbhrāntaṃ tu tad rakṣaḥ samare pratyadṛśyata cikṣepa colmukaṃ dīptam aśaniṃ jvalitām iva
english: "But the demon appeared unshaken in that battle and hurled back a blazing firebrand like a flaming thunderbolt."

sanskrit: tad udastam alātaṃ tu bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ padā savyena cikṣepa tad rakṣaḥ punar āvrajat
english: "But Bhīma, foremost among warriors, kicked away that hurled firebrand with his left foot; then the demon came at him again."

sanskrit: kirmīraś cāpi sahasā vṛkṣam utpāṭya pāṇḍavam daṇḍapāṇir iva kruddhaḥ samare pratyayudhyata
english: "And Kirmīra too, swiftly uprooting a tree, fought back against the Pāṇḍava in battle, like an enraged officer with his staff."

sanskrit: tad vṛkṣayuddham abhavan mahīruhavināśanam vālisugrīvayor bhrātror yathā śrīkāṅkṣiṇoḥ purā
english: "That battle with trees became a destruction of the forest, like the fight of the brothers Vālī and Sugrīva of old, each striving for glory."

sanskrit: śīrṣayoḥ patitā vṛkṣā bibhidur naikadhā tayoḥ yathaivotpalapadmāni mattayor dvipayos tathā
english: "Trees fell upon their heads and were broken in many pieces, just as lotus flowers and water-lilies are crushed between two rutting elephants."

sanskrit: muñjavaj jarjarībhūtā bahavas tatra pādapāḥ cīrāṇīva vyudastāni rejus tatra mahāvane
english: "Many trees there were shredded like munja grass, and lay scattered like torn rags across that great forest."

sanskrit: tad vṛkṣayuddham abhavat sumuhūrtaṃ viśāṃ pate rākṣasānāṃ ca mukhyasya narāṇām uttamasya ca
english: "That battle with trees lasted for a good while, O lord of the people, between the foremost of demons and the foremost of men."

sanskrit: tataḥ śilāṃ samutkṣipya bhīmasya yudhi tiṣṭhataḥ prāhiṇod rākṣasaḥ kruddho bhīmasenaś cacāla ha
english: "Then the enraged demon, lifting up a boulder, hurled it at Bhīma as he stood fighting; and Bhīmasena staggered."

sanskrit: taṃ śilātāḍanajaḍaṃ paryadhāvat sa rākṣasaḥ bāhuvikṣiptakiraṇaḥ svarbhānur iva bhāskaram
english: "The demon rushed around the Pāṇḍava stunned by the boulder-blow, his arms flung wide like rays, like Svarbhānu circling the sun."

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ samāśliṣya prakarṣantau parasparam ubhāv api cakāśete prayuddhau vṛṣabhāv iva
english: "They grappled with each other, each dragging at the other; both appeared as two bulls locked in combat."

sanskrit: tayor āsīt sutumulaḥ saṃprahāraḥ sudāruṇaḥ nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhavator vyāghrayor iva dṛptayoḥ
english: "Between them arose a most tumultuous and fearsome struggle, like that of two proud tigers armed with claws and fangs."

sanskrit: duryodhananikārāc ca bāhuvīryāc ca darpitaḥ kṛṣṇānayanadṛṣṭaś ca vyavardhata vṛkodaraḥ
english: "Swollen with pride at the insult dealt by Duryodhana, exulting in the strength of his arms, and his gaze fixed on Kṛṣṇā beside him, Vṛkodara grew in power."

sanskrit: abhipatyātha bāhubhyāṃ pratyagṛhṇād amarṣitaḥ mātaṅga iva mātaṅgaṃ prabhinnakaraṭāmukhaḥ
english: "Then he leaped forward and seized the demon with both arms, furious, like an elephant with split temples seizing another elephant."

sanskrit: taṃ cāpy ātha tato rakṣaḥ pratijagrāha vīryavān tam ākṣipad bhīmaseno balena balināṃ varaḥ
english: "And the powerful demon in turn grasped him; but Bhīmasena, foremost of the strong, flung him away by sheer force."

sanskrit: tayor bhujaviniṣpeṣād ubhayor balinos tadā śabdaḥ samabhavad ghoro veṇusphoṭasamo yudhi
english: "From the crashing together of the arms of those two powerful ones there arose a dreadful sound in battle, like the cracking of bamboo."

sanskrit: athainam ākṣipya balād gṛhya madhye vṛkodaraḥ dhūnayām āsa vegena vāyuś caṇḍa iva drumam
english: "Then Vṛkodara, forcibly seizing him and gripping him about the middle, shook him with violence like a fierce wind shaking a tree."

sanskrit: sa bhīmena parāmṛṣṭo durbalo balinā raṇe vyaspandata yathāprāṇaṃ vicakarṣa ca pāṇḍavam
english: "Seized by the mighty Bhīma in battle, the weakening demon thrashed about with whatever life remained in him and dragged at the Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: tata enaṃ pariśrāntam upalabhya vṛkodaraḥ yoktrayām āsa bāhubhyāṃ paśuṃ raśanayā yathā
english: "Then Vṛkodara, perceiving him to be exhausted, bound him with his arms as one binds a beast with a rope."

sanskrit: vinadantaṃ mahānādaṃ bhinnabherīsamasvanam bhrāmayām āsa suciraṃ visphurantam acetasam
english: "He swung him around for a long time as the demon roared with a great cry like the sound of a burst drum, struggling convulsively and losing consciousness."

sanskrit: taṃ viṣīdantam ājñāya rākṣasaṃ pāṇḍunandanaḥ pragṛhya tarasā dorbhyāṃ paśumāram amārayat
english: "Perceiving the demon to be sinking, the son of Pāṇḍu seized him swiftly with both arms and killed him as one kills a beast."

sanskrit: ākramya sa kaṭīdeśe jānunā rākṣasādhamam apīḍayata bāhubhyāṃ kaṇṭhaṃ tasya vṛkodaraḥ
english: "Vṛkodara pressed his knee into the loins of that vile demon and squeezed his throat with both arms."

sanskrit: atha taṃ jaḍasarvāṅgaṃ vyāvṛttanayanolbaṇam bhūtale pātayām āsa vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha
english: "Then he cast him down upon the ground, all his limbs numb and his eyes rolling hideously, and spoke these words:"

sanskrit: hiḍimbabakayoḥ pāpa na tvam aśrupramārjanam kariṣyasi gataś cāsi yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: "'You wretch, you shall not wipe away the tears for Hiḍimba and Baka — you are bound for the abode of Yama.'"

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā puruṣapravīras; taṃ rākṣasaṃ krodhavivṛttanetraḥ prasrastavastrābharaṇaṃ sphurantam; udbhrāntacittaṃ vyasum utsasarja
english: "Having spoken thus, that foremost of men, his eyes wide with wrath, released the demon whose garments and ornaments had slipped away, who was still twitching, his mind gone, and whose life had departed."

sanskrit: tasmin hate toyadatulyarūpe; kṛṣṇāṃ puraskṛtya narendraputrāḥ bhīmaṃ praśasyātha guṇair anekair; hṛṣṭās tato dvaitavanāya jagmuḥ
english: "When that demon resembling a rain cloud was slain, the sons of the king of men, placing Kṛṣṇā before them, praised Bhīma with many virtues and then, glad of heart, proceeded to the Dvaita forest."

sanskrit: evaṃ vinihataḥ saṃkhye kirmīro manujādhipa bhīmena vacanāt tasya dharmarājasya kaurava
english: "Thus was Kirmīra slain in battle, O lord of men, by Bhīma, at the word of that Dharma-king, O Kaurava."

sanskrit: tato niṣkaṇṭakaṃ kṛtvā vanaṃ tad aparājitaḥ draupadyā saha dharmajño vasatiṃ tām uvāsa ha
english: "Then the undefeated knower of dharma, having rid that forest of its thorn, dwelt there together with Draupadī."

sanskrit: samāśvāsya ca te sarve draupadīṃ bharatarṣabhāḥ prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ prītyā praśaśaṃsur vṛkodaram
english: "And all those bulls among Bhāratas, having comforted Draupadī, with gladdened hearts joyfully praised Vṛkodara."

sanskrit: bhīmabāhubalotpiṣṭe vinaṣṭe rākṣase tataḥ viviśus tad vanaṃ vīrāḥ kṣemaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam
english: "With the demon crushed by the arm-strength of Bhīma and destroyed, the heroes then entered that forest, now safe and free of its thorn."
